title: Resting-ECG context modestly improves a frozen exercise-ST model across centers, but not robust prediction under training uncertainty
abstract: A literature-led interaction between exercise ST depression and any abnormal resting ECG was added to a flexible standard-measure logistic model trained in 303 Cleveland patients and tested without target tuning in 293 Hungarian patients. Target Brier score decreased from0.16534 to0.16102 (gain0.00432; joint source-refit/target-bootstrap95% interval -0.00603 to0.01357). Source cross-validation gain was0.00022. Abnormal-ECG target patients worsened despite an overall gain, and resting-ECG subtype distributions differed substantially. Stronger regularization reduced the gain to0.00042, and a linear standard-measure baseline outperformed the primary augmented model. This is a conditional cross-center prediction observation, not a reliable new biomarker or clinical advantage; the cohorts were previously used for other worker studies.
